 COMMON JUDGMENT  These petitions are filed under Section 166 of M.V.
Act, seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- in MVC 4069/2021 and Rs.20,00,000/- in MVC 4070/2021 from respondents on account of grievous injuries sustained by petitioners in Road Traffic Accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitions are that, on 03- 09-2021 at about 3.15 p.m., near guddahatti Gate,
NH-7, Hosur-Bengaluru road, Bengaluru, petitioners were traveling in motorcycle, bearing No.KA-53-ED- 8754 slowly, carefully, cautiously observing all traffic rules and regulations, at that time the driver of lorry,
bearing No.GJ-27-TT-7898 drove the same with high speed, rash and negligent manner so as to endangering  3 (SCCH-16) MVC 4069/2021  & 4070/2021 human life and property came from behind and dashed against petitioners' motorcycle.

Due to the impact,
petitioners fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over their body.
Immediately after the accident, they were shifted to Sri Sai Hospital, wherein they took treatment as an inpatient.
2(a). Earlier to the accident, petitioner in MVC 4069/2021 was working as tailor and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she became permanently disabled and whereby lost her earning capacity.

2(b). Earlier to the accident, petitioner in MVC In Smt. Bhagyamma vs In 1. National Insurance Co. Ltd on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33308953/
2 4070/2021 was working as mason and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.

sentences.text: Discharge summary, which is at Ex.P8 shows that the petitioner had taken treatment as an inpatient for a period of 19 days in Sri Sai Hospital and underwent surgery.
It is averred that because of the injuries she suffered the disablement and from which she lost or lessen her earning capacity.

In proof of the disablement she examined PW3 - Consultant Neurosurgeon from Padmashree Diagnostics, who assessed the disability of petitioner, opined that the petitioner suffered permanent whole body disability at 61% to 80%.
His evidences clear that he is not the treated doctor.

Petitioner had maxillary fracture only,
and for other injuries she had conservative treatment only.
The doctor is not exact on the disability.
Over all cross-examination of the doctor shows the disability assessed was in the higher side.

As per the elicitation from this doctor from the learned counsel for Respondent No.1 50% of minimum disability in assessed disability is taken to be considered, which  10 (SCCH-16) MVC 4069/2021  & 4070/2021 would meet ends of justice.
No particular evidence by Ophthalmologist and Orthopaedician is significant to note here.
G.C.S of the petitioner was normal at the time of discharge from the hospital is considered.
S.A.H., S.D.H and D.A.I came to be healed on conservative treatment.
There was no injury to LOBE is perceived.
Brain stem and Cerebellum were normal are considered.
There was no Craniotomy is taken into consideration.
In the discharge summary there is nothing about the movements of eyes.
There is no Neurology deficit.

There is no clinical investigation regarding injury of the optic nerve and finally the petitioner herself stepped into the witness box,
adduced her examination in chief and faced the cross examinations are taken into consideration.
In view of all these important aspects the evidence of PW-3 remains only supportive rather his expertized opinion and the exaggeration in his opinion is apparent.

Under the facts and circumstances of case and having regard to the nature of injuries and those being healed, the disability to the whole body is considered at half of minimum assessment made by the doctor i.e.,
30.5% as disablement as the disability assessed is an opinion of the doctor and no certificate of disability is produced from the competent authority.

sentences.text: However, no document is forthcoming regarding avocation of petitioner is concerned.

hence in the present case, avocation of petitioner is need to be considered notionally as she had notional income only.
Age
As per Ex.P13 - aadhar card, date of birth of petitioner was 10-07-1971 and so that, age of petitioner was 50 years at the time of incident.
Hence, it is considered.
Income
As discussed on the head of avocation, the petitioner's avocation taken to be considered notionally.
In this regard as per the resolution of hon'ble the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, dated 17-02- 2022 notional income for the year 2021 came to be fixed at Rs.15,000/.
In the present case, under the facts and circumstances of case, Rs.15,000/- is taken to be considered as notional income of the petitioner, per month.
Considering the avocation and income notionally now loss of future income due to disability needs to be calculated.
According to the determined age of  12 (SCCH-16) MVC 4069/2021  & 4070/2021 petitioner multiplier is 13.
So, 30.5% of monthly notional income comes to Rs.4,575/- x 12 months x multiplier 13 = Rs.7,13,700/- is considered as compensation under the head of loss of future income due to the disablement.
Laid up period and Pain and sufferings  Petitioner was treated as inpatient from 03-09- 2021 to 21-09-2021.
She underwent operation.
She suffered fracture.
So that, she suffered pains and sufferings and also lost her earnings at the time of her treatment as well as her nourishment at least for the period of 4 months.

It is therefore, it is just and proper to award compensation considering her pains and In Smt. Bhagyamma vs In 1. National Insurance Co. Ltd on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33308953/
8 sufferings and for her laid up period.

Liability:
 23.
Insurance policy and its validity are admitted and no breaches are established by the insurer.
As found on the discussions on issue No.1, the negligence was on the part of driver of the lorry.
On vicarious liability respondent No.2 being the owner of the lorry is responsible, respondent No.1 being the insurer of respondent No.2 contractually liable to pay compensation.
Thus, respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay such compensation.
However, initially respondent No.1 is liable to pay the determined compensation.
The petitioners are only entitled to such compensation and not fully as claimed for.
Accordingly, this issue stands answered partly in the affirmative in both the cases.
ISSUE No.3 OF BOTH THE CASES:
24 . In view of the findings, both petitions deserve to be allowed in part.

Hence, the following order is passed:
 ORDER
Petitions in MVC No.4069/2021 and 4070/2021 are partly allowed with costs.

Petitioner in MVC 4069/2021 is entitled to compensation of 18 (SCCH-16) MVC 4069/2021 &
4070/2021 Rs.16,75,600/- (Rupees sixteen lakhs, seventy five thousand and six hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
Petitioner in MVC 4070/2021 is entitled to compensation of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees ten thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.1 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner in MVC 4069/2021, 25% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in her name as FD in any nationalized bank for the period of two years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 75% amount with proportionate interest shall be released 19 (SCCH-16) MVC 4069/2021 & 4070/2021 to her through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest awarded to the petitioner in MVC 4070/2021 shall be released to him through E-payment on proper identification and verification.

 ORDER
Petitions in MVC No.4069/2021 and 4070/2021 are partly allowed with costs.
Petitioner in MVC 4069/2021 is entitled to compensation of 18 (SCCH-16) MVC 4069/2021 &
4070/2021 Rs.16,75,600/- (Rupees sixteen lakhs, seventy five thousand and six hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
Petitioner in MVC 4070/2021 is entitled to compensation of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees ten thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.

Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner in MVC 4069/2021, 25% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in her name as FD in any nationalized bank for the period of two years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 75% amount with proportionate interest shall be released 19 (SCCH-16) MVC 4069/2021 & 4070/2021 to her through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest awarded to the petitioner in MVC 4070/2021 shall be released to him through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/- each in both the cases.
Draw award accordingly in both the cases.
